tagline: Ghats, Ganga aarti and street food in one of the world's oldest living cities
signatureFood: kachori sabzi, tamatar chaat, malaiyo, banarasi paan, thandai

seasons.label: Cool season
seasons.note: Best time to visit; pleasant for boat rides, though winter mornings can be foggy and cold.

seasons.label: Hot season
seasons.note: Very hot; visit ghats at dawn and dusk and avoid midday walks.

seasons.label: Monsoon
seasons.note: The Ganga floods the lower ghats and boat rides may be suspended; humid with frequent rain.

places.name: Sunrise Boat Ride on the Ganges
places.desc: Dawn boat ride along the ghats to see morning rituals, bathers and the waking riverfront.

places.name: Evening Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat
places.desc: Nightly fire ritual with priests, lamps and chanting on the main ghat; arrive early for a good spot.

places.name: Kashi Vishwanath Temple and Corridor
places.desc: One of the twelve Jyotirlinga temples; expect security checks and queues, and go early.

places.name: Sarnath Buddhist Site and Museum
places.desc: Where the Buddha gave his first sermon, with the Dhamek Stupa, ruins and an archaeological museum.

places.name: Assi Ghat Morning Walk
places.desc: Youthful southern ghat with morning yoga, classical music mornings and riverside cafes.

places.name: BHU and Bharat Kala Bhavan
places.desc: Sprawling university campus with Bharat Kala Bhavan, which has miniature paintings and sculpture.

places.name: Ramnagar Fort
places.desc: 18th-century riverside fort of the Kashi Naresh, with a museum of vintage cars, weapons and costumes.

places.name: Banarasi Street Food Crawl
places.desc: Tasting walk through old-city lanes for kachori sabzi, tamatar chaat, blue lassi and malaiyo.

places.name: Banarasi Silk Weaving and Shopping
places.desc: Visit a handloom workshop and showrooms for Banarasi silk sarees and brocades; prices depend on what you buy.

places.name: Durga Temple and Tulsi Manas Temple
places.desc: Two historic temples near Durgakund, one for the goddess and the other tied to the author of the Ramcharitmanas.
